# Modules {#sec-modules}

This page lists the addons that carry module functions. Each function file is
`functions/fnc_<name>.sqf`. Functions use the name
`aee_<component>_fnc_<name>`.

## core

The orchestrator. It initialises the mod, registers the EDEN module, updates
the environment, and reports diagnostics.

It also reports module health and runs the throttled cross-module
consistency monitor. The monitor reads the published producer values, calls
the pure `evaluateConsistency` kernel and logs one warning per failing
invariant. The design decision is in ADR-020.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `calculateSeededWeatherProgression` | Compute a deterministic weather quality factor from a seeded LCG |
| `deterministicRandom` | Generate a deterministic pseudo-random value from two integer seeds |
| `diagnostic` | Report diagnostic information |
| `init` | Initialise the mod at mission start |
| `moduleInit` | Initialise the EDEN module |
| `moduleStormInit` | Initialise the storm control EDEN module |
| `updateEnvironment` | Orchestrate the environment update |

### Human-vision perception model

The model derives the normal-vision tone, contrast, white balance and mesopic
tint from published human-vision science. It subsumes the aesthetic base grade
in place and reuses the registry keys `BaseGrade` and `BaseAcuity`. The design
decision is in ADR-014.

The perception monitor folds the published view state into one fixed schema.
`perceptionSample` is a pure kernel that reads no world state, so the local
driver and an AI caller use the same entry point. The client driver
`perceptionUpdate` reads the state each half second, publishes the aggregate
and its named fields, emits one human line, and calls `perceptionDetectDeviation`
to set the deviation flags. The monitor is client only. It self-gates on
`hasInterface` and on a living local player, so a dedicated server publishes
nothing. The design decision is in ADR-020.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `perceptionChromaticAdaptation` | Derive the partial von Kries blend toward the display white |
| `perceptionIlluminant` | Normalise the scene illuminant to unit luma |
| `perceptionMesopicColor` | Derive the mesopic desaturation and Purkinje colorize slot |
| `perceptionParams` | Compose the tone and colour stages into the display arrays |
| `perceptionToneResponse` | Derive display brightness, contrast and offset from the adapted luminance |

### MGRS positioning and the signal tracker

The MGRS layer maps a world position to a full grid reference. The anchor is
read once from `CfgWorlds` and cached. The chain is world position to the
anchor box, then to UTM, then to MGRS. The HUD grid line, the map overlay and
the GPS readout consume the same kernel.

The signal tracker replaces the exact friendly position with a modelled one.
It applies the GNSS error-ellipse, fix-state and datalink kernels to the
local group, then draws fuzzy markers with an uncertainty ellipse. The design
decision is recorded in ADR-022.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `formatGridDisplay` | Return the MGRS grid line, or the legacy numeric grid |
| `mgrsGridLines` | Plan the MGRS grid overlay for a visible world rectangle |
| `mgrsCursorText` | Format the MGRS reference and elevation at the map cursor |
| `mgrsMapDraw` | Draw the MGRS grid, the cursor readout, the player and the AEE-owned markers |
| `mgrsMarkerText` | Format a marker position as MGRS for the diary text |
| `gpsBuild` / `gpsUpdate` | Draw the GPS device readout, gated on an `ItemGPS` item |
| `trackerProject` | Displace the exact position by the modelled error |
| `trackerUpdate` | Survey the group and publish the tracker state |
| `trackerDraw` | Draw the fuzzy markers and the error ellipse |

The tracker probes what engine icon suppression allows. The
`disableMapIndicators` call is local and suppresses the engine friendly map
indicators only where the difficulty exposes extended map content. The
`setGroupIconsVisible` call affects only the High Command icons and never the
default engine markers. The tracker draws its own markers in both cases.

### NATO/OPFOR map symbology

The symbology layer registers real engine map markers. Each symbol is a
`CfgMarkers` entry with a real `.paa` icon, so it is selectable in the marker
dialog, placeable in Eden and drawn by the engine marker layer. The frame shape
and the colour show the affiliation, the dimension modifier shows the battle
dimension, and the inner glyph shows the function. The design decision is in
ADR-023.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `symbolCategory` | Map an engine marker type or vehicle class to a class category |
| `symbolPalette` | Map an affiliation and the palette to the Table 1-4 colour |
| `symbolFrame` | Build the frame outline for an affiliation and a dimension |
| `symbolIcon` | Build the inner glyph for a class category |
| `symbologyMarkerType` | Map an affiliation and a category to the CfgMarkers type |
| `symbologyMarkerColor` | Map an affiliation and a palette to the CfgMarkerColors class |
| `symbolResolve` | Resolve the inputs to one marker specification |
| `symbologyMarkerCategory` | Read a marker and map it to a class category |
| `symbologyUnitCategory` | Read a unit and map it to a class category |
| `symbologyAffiliation` | Read a marker colour and resolve the affiliation |
| `symbologyPaletteFriendly` | Resolve the Auto palette against the local side |
| `symbologyMarkers` | Apply the AEE markers on the map open and close |
| `symbologyMarkersApply` | Convert the mission and unit markers locally |
| `symbologyMarkersRestore` | Restore the converted markers on map close |
| `symbologyWorldDraw` | Draw the real marker texture in the 3D world |

The engine 3D unit icons cannot be suppressed, so the world layer draws over
them and states the ceiling. The map layer converts the engine mission markers
to AEE markers locally and restores them when the map closes.

The engine's own NATO texture is referenced where it fits
(`\A3\ui_f\data\map\markers\nato\b_inf.paa`). AEE produces the rest under
`addons/symbology/data/markers/`, so no third-party texture is vendored.

### World lighting matcher

The matcher classifies each world from published facts and drives the star
render scale, the night factor, the grain scale and the haze scale. It consults
no map name. The design decision is in ADR-016.

| Function | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `applyWorldLighting` | Run the matcher once per environment tick and publish the profile |
| `worldLightingClass` | Derive the climate class from biome, latitude and terrain signals |
| `worldLightingProfile` | Derive the four bounded scales from the class and the weather |

## wildlife

The client-local ecology. It reads the biome, the time, the weather, the
water, the terrain and the disturbance field. It plays a vanilla sound bed
that reacts to quiet approach, flight spooks and gunfire, and it spawns
client-local animals by biome and terrain. Hunger and thirst move them
between water and grazing ground. It reuses vanilla classes and vanilla
media only.

### Wildlife ecology

The ecology layer makes each animal read the real conditions around it and
decide from them. It is client-local and reads published `aee_*` state only.
The species rules are a cited data corpus under `data/wildlife/`, generated
into `addons/wildlife/data/ecology_corpus.sqf` and matched, never branched in
SQF. The per-constant register is
`docs/wiki/research/wildlife-ecology-constants.md`.

The layer has four parts.

- **Match.** `getSpeciesMatch` matches the Koppen family, the true sun
  elevation in degrees, the air temperature, the month, the water, the
  vegetation, the surface material and the weather, and returns weighted
  species-group rows. `getCallPattern` and `getSeason` give the temporal and
  seasonal shape.
- **Environment.** `sampleNeighbourhood` walks a budgeted local grid and
  returns the foliage fraction, the surface votes, the water fraction, the
  structure fraction and the mean elevation. `environmentSuitability` scores a
  group against the sample. `habitatBoundary` keeps an animal in its patch with
  a rare seeded excursion. `environmentGrid` owns the bounded, aged per-cell
  cache.
- **Cognition.** `wildlifePerceive`, `wildlifeThink` and `ecologyTick` run
  perceive, think, act and recover over the `aee_ai` substrate on a count and
  millisecond budget with a front re-queue.
- **Communication.** `callEmit` types a call and gives it an urgency.
  `callReceive` decodes a heard call into a response. `callPublish` and
  `callSample` own the bounded, decayed heard-call bus.

The acoustic layer models sound events, not the engine `Fired` flag.
`acousticSourceDb` gives the source levels, `acousticLevel` propagates them
with distance, occlusion and air absorption, and `acousticPublish` and
`acousticSample` own the event bus. `shotAudio` derives the muzzle report, the
supersonic crack, the near-pass snap and the ricochet from the real
ballistics. `callPitch` gives the Doppler and species pitch, and `emitterPlan`
keeps the attached emitters bounded.

| Function | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `acousticLevel` | Propagate sound events to one listener as a continuous level |
| `acousticOccluders` | Collect the bounded occluders on the source-listener line |
| `acousticPublish` | Append a sound event to the bounded, aged event bus |
| `acousticSample` | Read the propagated level of the live events at a listener |
| `acousticSourceDb` | Map a sound-event kind to its source level |
| `callEmit` | Type a call and give it an urgency from a condition |
| `callPitch` | Return the Doppler and species pitch multiplier for a call |
| `callPublish` | Append a heard call to the bounded, decayed bus |
| `callReceive` | Decode a heard call into a conspecific response |
| `callSample` | Read the strongest live call at a cell |
| `ecologyBudget` | Decide whether another animal may be ticked this call |
| `ecologyTick` | Run perceive, think, act and recover on a budget |
| `emitterClass` | Resolve the looping source for one sound group |
| `emitterPlan` | Choose which animals create, keep or release an emitter |
| `emitterRelease` | Delete one attached emitter and free its source |
| `emitterSync` | Attach and bound the emitters for the active animals |
| `environmentGrid` | Age and cap the per-cell environment cache |
| `environmentSuitability` | Score a species group against an environment sample |
| `getCallPattern` | Return the calling probability for one time bin |
| `getSeason` | Return the season enum and the seasonality factor |
| `getSpeciesMatch` | Match species groups from the environment and the time |
| `habitatBoundary` | Keep an animal in its patch with a rare seeded excursion |
| `pickBedSource` | Draw one ambient bed source over all matching rows |
| `shotAudio` | Derive the report, crack, snap and ricochet from the ballistics |
| `soundTick` | Schedule the species calls for one time bin |
| `speciesSound` | Map a species group to the vanilla media that exist |
| `wildlifePerceive` | Fold the environment and the state into a perception vector |
| `wildlifeThink` | Map the perception into an action, a call plan and a movement |

present.
